simple.meaning: דׇּרְבוֹן (dorbôwn) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a goad.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in 1 Samuel, Ecclesiastes, beginning at 1 Samuel 13:21. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דׇּרְבוֹן (H1861) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: דׇּרְבוֹן (dorbôwn) / H1861 is traced through 1 Samuel 13:21, Ecclesiastes 12:11 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1861. dorbown דָּרְבָן noun [masculine] goad (Late Hebrew id. ), הַדָּרְבָ֑ן לְהַצִּיב 1Sam 13:21 (on form compare Ol § 215 b. 3 and others Dr). [ דָּֽרְבֹנָה ] noun [feminine] goad , only absolute plural, in simile כַּדָּ֣רְבֹנוֺת חֲכָמִים דִּבְרֵי Eccl 12:11 (compare De Koh 434 ). דרג (√ of following compare Arabic go on foot, step by step, walk , rise in grade, rank ; Late Hebrew דרג Hiph`il raise, make high ; Ethiopic is be connected ; Aramaic (verb denominative according to PS); also Assyrian darâgu , be high , lift , Lyon Sargontexte 80 , durgu, daragu, path, way (of steep mountain paths) COT Gloss (compare also דרך ); Arabic a step, stair , Aramaic דַּרְגָּא , , , id. )

occurrences.englishText: The price was one payim† A payim (or pim) was 2/3 shekel of silver, or 0.26 ounces, or 7.6 grams each to sharpen mattocks, plowshares, pitchforks, axes, and goads.
The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
